rules.name: check
rules.source:
check(Ctx, check(Checker, KingSq, Checkers)) :-
    piece(Ctx, Owner, king, KingSq),
    opponent(Owner, Checker),
    attackers(Ctx, Checker, KingSq, Checkers),
    Checkers \== []
rules.summary: A king is attacked by at least one enemy piece.

rules.name: pin
rules.source:
pin(Ctx, pin(Kind, PC, PT, PSq, T, Sq, BT, BSq)) :-
    piece(Ctx, PC, PT, PSq),
    slider_dir(PT, Dir),
    ctx_assoc(Ctx, Assoc),
    first_on_ray(Assoc, PSq, Dir, Sq, C-T),
    opponent(PC, C),
    T \== king,
    first_on_ray(Assoc, Sq, Dir, BSq, C-BT),
    pin_kind(Ctx, C, PT, PSq, T, Sq, BT, BSq, Kind),
    \+ harmless_pin(Kind, T, Dir)
rules.summary: A slider looks through exactly one enemy piece at a more valuable one.

rules.name: skewer
rules.source:
skewer(Ctx, skewer(PC, PT, PSq, FT, FSq, BT, BSq)) :-
    piece(Ctx, PC, PT, PSq),
    slider_dir(PT, Dir),
    ctx_assoc(Ctx, Assoc),
    first_on_ray(Assoc, PSq, Dir, FSq, C-FT),
    opponent(PC, C),
    first_on_ray(Assoc, FSq, Dir, BSq, C-BT),
    BT \== king, BT \== pawn,
    value(FT, VF), value(BT, VB), value(PT, VP),
    VF > VB, VF > VP,
    ( VB > VP ; \+ attacked_by(Ctx, C, BSq) ),
    % ...and the piece in front must not simply be able to take the attacker for nothing
    \+ ( attack(Ctx, C, FT, FSq, PSq), \+ attacked_by(Ctx, PC, PSq) )
rules.summary: Like a pin, but the valuable piece is in front and must move away.

rules.name: fork
rules.source:
fork(Ctx, fork(C, T, From, Targets)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, T, From),
    T \== king,
    opponent(C, O),
    findall(TT-TSq,
            ( attack(Ctx, C, T, From, TSq),
              at(Ctx, TSq, O, TT),
              fork_target(Ctx, T, O, TT, TSq)
            ),
            Targets),
    Targets = [_, _|_],
    safe_piece(Ctx, C, T, From)
rules.summary: One piece attacks two or more enemy pieces that each matter, and cannot simply be taken for free itself.

rules.name: hanging
rules.source:
hanging(Ctx, hanging(C, T, Sq, Attackers)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, T, Sq),
    is_hanging(Ctx, C, T, Sq),
    opponent(C, O),
    findall(AT-ASq, can_capture(Ctx, O, AT, ASq, Sq), Attackers)
rules.summary: A piece that nothing defends and that an enemy piece is able to take.

rules.name: threatened
rules.source:
threatened(Ctx, threatened(C, T, Sq, AT, ASq)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, T, Sq),
    attacked_by(Ctx, C, Sq),             % defended (otherwise it is "hanging")
    once(threatened_by(Ctx, C, T, Sq, AT, ASq))
rules.summary: A defended piece attacked by something cheaper than itself.

rules.name: overloaded
rules.source:
overloaded(Ctx, overloaded(C, T, Sq, Guarded)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, T, Sq),
    T \== king,
    opponent(C, O),
    findall(GSq,
            ( piece(Ctx, C, GT, GSq),
              GT \== king, GT \== pawn,
              GSq \== Sq,
              attacked_by(Ctx, O, GSq),
              attackers(Ctx, C, GSq, [_-Sq])
            ),
            Guarded),
    Guarded = [_, _|_]
rules.summary: A piece that is the only defender of two or more attacked friends.

rules.name: battery
rules.source:
battery(Ctx, battery(C, FT, FSq, BT, BSq, TT, TSq)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, BT, BSq),
    slider_dir(BT, Dir),
    toward_enemy(C, Dir),
    ctx_assoc(Ctx, Assoc),
    first_on_ray(Assoc, BSq, Dir, FSq, C-FT),
    once(slider_dir(FT, Dir)),
    first_on_ray(Assoc, FSq, Dir, TSq, O-TT),
    opponent(C, O)
rules.summary: Two line pieces of one colour, one behind the other on a line both of them move along, bearing on an enemy piece. Without a target (a queen and rook side by side on the back rank, say) it is not worth reporting.

rules.name: discovered_attack
rules.source:
discovered_attack(Ctx, discovered_attack(C, MT, MSq, ST, SSq, TT, TSq)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, ST, SSq),
    slider_dir(ST, Dir),
    ctx_assoc(Ctx, Assoc),
    first_on_ray(Assoc, SSq, Dir, MSq, C-MT),
    \+ slider_dir(MT, Dir),              % that would be a battery, not a mask
    \+ pawn_stays_on_line(MT, Dir),
    first_on_ray(Assoc, MSq, Dir, TSq, O-TT),
    opponent(C, O),
    discovered_target(Ctx, ST, O, TT, TSq),
    \+ target_strikes_first(Ctx, C, ST, SSq, TT, Dir)
rules.summary: A line piece is masked by one of its own men, and behind that man stands an enemy piece worth hitting. If the masking piece moves off the line, the attack appears; if it moves with a threat of its own, both land at once.

rules.name: pinned_defender
rules.source:
pinned_defender(Ctx, pinned_defender(C, T, Sq, GT, GSq)) :-
    pin(Ctx, pin(absolute, PC, _, PSq, T, Sq, _, _)),
    opponent(PC, C),
    piece(Ctx, C, GT, GSq),
    GT \== king,
    GSq \== Sq,
    attacked_by(Ctx, PC, GSq),
    attackers(Ctx, C, GSq, [_-Sq]),
    \+ collinear(PSq, Sq, GSq)
rules.summary: A piece pinned to its king is the only defender of an attacked friend, so that friend is really undefended. (If the friend stands on the pin line itself the pinned piece may still recapture along it: not reported.)

rules.name: trapped
rules.source:
trapped(Ctx, trapped(C, T, Sq, AT, ASq)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, T, Sq),
    memberchk(T, [knight, bishop, rook, queen]),
    opponent(C, O),
    (   threatened_by(Ctx, C, T, Sq, AT, ASq)
    ->  true
    ;   is_hanging(Ctx, C, T, Sq),
        once(attack(Ctx, O, AT, ASq, Sq))
    ),
    \+ ( attack(Ctx, C, T, Sq, To),
         \+ at(Ctx, To, C, _),
         safe_destination(Ctx, C, T, Sq, To)
       )
rules.summary: A piece under attack with nowhere safe to go.

rules.name: open_file
rules.source:
open_file(Ctx, open_file(F)) :-
    once(( has_heavy_piece(Ctx, white) ; has_heavy_piece(Ctx, black) )),
    once(piece(Ctx, _, pawn, _)),
    between(1, 8, F),
    is_open_file(Ctx, F)
rules.summary: Files only matter while someone still has a rook or queen to put on them. With no pawns left at all every file is "open" and the fact says nothing.

rules.name: semi_open_file
rules.source:
semi_open_file(Ctx, semi_open_file(C, F)) :-
    opponent(C, _),
    has_heavy_piece(Ctx, C),
    between(1, 8, F),
    is_semi_open_file(Ctx, C, F)
rules.summary: A file with no pawn of one colour and at least one of the other, reported while that colour still has a rook or queen to use it.

rules.name: passed_pawn
rules.source:
passed_pawn(Ctx, passed_pawn(C, Sq)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, pawn, Sq),
    is_passed(Ctx, C, Sq)
rules.summary: A pawn with no enemy pawn ahead of it on its own file or either file beside it.

rules.name: isolated_pawn
rules.source:
isolated_pawn(Ctx, isolated_pawn(C, F/R)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F/R),
    \+ ( piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F1/_), abs(F1 - F) =:= 1 )
rules.summary: A pawn with no friendly pawn on either neighbouring file.

rules.name: doubled_pawns
rules.source:
doubled_pawns(Ctx, doubled_pawns(C, F, Sqs)) :-
    opponent(C, _),
    between(1, 8, F),
    findall(F/R, piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F/R), Sqs),
    Sqs = [_, _|_]
rules.summary: Two or more pawns of one colour on the same file.

rules.name: weak_square
rules.source:
weak_square(Ctx, weak_square(Owner, Sq, Support)) :-
    opponent(Owner, _),
    is_weak_square(Ctx, Owner, Sq, Support)
rules.summary: A central square on the owner's third or fourth rank that no pawn of the owner can ever attack again and that an enemy pawn already controls.

rules.name: king_shield
rules.source:
king_shield(Ctx, king_shield(C, F/R, Missing)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, king, F/R),
    rel_rank(C, R, 1),
    memberchk(F, [1, 2, 3, 7, 8]),
    Lo is max(1, F - 1), Hi is min(8, F + 1),
    findall(SF,
            ( between(Lo, Hi, SF),
              \+ ( piece(Ctx, C, pawn, SF/PR),
                   rel_rank(C, PR, PRR),
                   PRR =< 3
                 )
            ),
            Missing),
    Missing \== []
rules.summary: A castled-looking king (wing files, back rank) with pawns missing in front.

rules.name: weak_back_rank
rules.source:
weak_back_rank(Ctx, weak_back_rank(C, F/R)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, king, F/R),
    rel_rank(C, R, 1),
    opponent(C, O),
    has_heavy_piece(Ctx, O),
    rel_rank(C, R2, 2),
    Lo is max(1, F - 1), Hi is min(8, F + 1),
    forall(between(Lo, Hi, F2), at(Ctx, F2/R2, C, _)),
    \+ ( piece(Ctx, C, T, _/R), memberchk(T, [rook, queen]) )
rules.summary: The king sits on its back rank behind a wall of its own men, with no rook or queen of its own on that rank, while the enemy still has a heavy piece: a check along the rank could be mate.

rules.name: outpost_piece
rules.source:
outpost_piece(Ctx, outpost_piece(C, T, Sq, Support)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, T, Sq),
    memberchk(T, [knight, bishop]),
    opponent(C, O),
    is_weak_square(Ctx, O, Sq, Support)
rules.summary: A knight or bishop already standing on a hole in the enemy camp.

rules.name: backward_pawn
rules.source:
backward_pawn(Ctx, backward_pawn(C, F/R)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F/R),
    rel_rank(C, R, RR),
    once(( piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F1/_), abs(F1 - F) =:= 1 )),
    \+ ( piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F2/R2),
         abs(F2 - F) =:= 1,
         rel_rank(C, R2, RR2),
         RR2 =< RR
       ),
    step(C, R, R1),
    opponent(C, O),
    once(attack(Ctx, O, pawn, _, F/R1))
rules.summary: A pawn whose neighbours have all gone past it, so none can support its advance, and whose next square is covered by an enemy pawn.

rules.name: rook_on_seventh
rules.source:
rook_on_seventh(Ctx, rook_on_seventh(C, F/R)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, rook, F/R),
    rel_rank(C, R, 7),
    opponent(C, O),
    (   piece(Ctx, O, king, _/KR), rel_rank(C, KR, 8)
    ->  true
    ;   piece(Ctx, O, pawn, _/R)
    ->  true
    )
rules.summary: A rook on the seventh rank that has something to do there: the enemy king is cut off on its back rank, or there are pawns to attack.

rules.name: pawn_majority
rules.source:
pawn_majority(Ctx, pawn_majority(C, Wing, Sqs, M)) :-
    opponent(C, O),
    member(Wing-Files, [queenside-[1, 2, 3], kingside-[6, 7, 8]]),
    findall(F/R, ( piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F/R), memberchk(F, Files) ), Sqs),
    findall(x, ( piece(Ctx, O, pawn, F/_), memberchk(F, Files) ), Theirs),
    length(Sqs, N),
    length(Theirs, M),
    M >= 1,
    N > M
rules.summary: More pawns than the opponent on one wing (the opponent having at least one there): the raw material for a passed pawn.

rules.name: pawn_break
rules.source:
pawn_break(Ctx, pawn_break(C, F/R, F/R1, Target)) :-
    ctx_side(Ctx, C),
    piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F/R),
    between(3, 6, F),
    pawn_advance(Ctx, C, F/R, R1),
    opponent(C, O),
    step(C, R1, R2),
    once(( member(DF, [-1, 1]),
           TF is F + DF,
           Target = TF/R2,
           at(Ctx, Target, O, pawn)
         ))
rules.summary: The side to move has a centre or bishop-file pawn that can advance (one square, or two from its starting square) to a square from which it attacks an enemy pawn.

rules.name: unstoppable_pawn
rules.source:
unstoppable_pawn(Ctx, unstoppable_pawn(C, F/R)) :-
    piece(Ctx, C, pawn, F/R),
    is_passed(Ctx, C, F/R),
    opponent(C, O),
    \+ ( piece(Ctx, O, T, _), T \== king, T \== pawn ),
    \+ ( piece(Ctx, _, _, F/RA), ahead(C, R, RA) ),
    rel_rank(C, R, RR0),
    RR is max(RR0, 3),                   % from its starting square it may jump two
    Moves is 8 - RR,
    rel_rank(C, QR, 8),
    piece(Ctx, O, king, KF/KR),
    KingMoves is max(abs(KF - F), abs(KR - QR)),
    ctx_side(Ctx, Side),
    (   Side == C
    ->  KingMoves > Moves
    ;   KingMoves - 1 > Moves
    )
rules.summary: The rule of the square. A passed pawn with a clear path, against a king and pawns only, queens by force when the enemy king is too far away to reach the queening square in time.

rules.name: gives_check
rules.source:
motif(_, After, C, _, _, motif(gives_check, 300, [KSq], check)) :-
    opponent(C, O),
    piece(After, O, king, KSq),
    attacked_by(After, C, KSq)
rules.summary: After the move the enemy king is attacked.

rules.name: captures_hanging
rules.source:
motif(Root, _, C, _, To, motif(captures_hanging, Score, [To], captured(T))) :-
    opponent(C, O),
    at(Root, To, O, T),
    is_hanging(Root, O, T, To),
    value(T, V),
    Score is 150 * V
rules.summary: The move takes a piece that was undefended before the move.

rules.name: wins_exchange
rules.source:
motif(Root, _, C, From, To, motif(wins_exchange, Score, [To], exchange(MT, T))) :-
    opponent(C, O),
    at(Root, To, O, T),
    \+ is_hanging(Root, O, T, To),
    at(Root, From, C, MT),
    value(T, VT), value(MT, VM),
    VT > VM,
    Score is 100 * (VT - VM)
rules.summary: The move takes a defended piece worth more than the piece that takes it.

rules.name: creates_fork
rules.source:
motif(_, After, C, _, To, motif(creates_fork, 400, Squares, fork(T, To, Targets))) :-
    at(After, To, C, T),
    fork(After, fork(C, T, To, Targets)),
    pairs_values(Targets, Squares)
rules.summary: Where it lands, the moved piece forks: the same rule that reports a fork in a position, applied to the position after the move.

rules.name: creates_pin
rules.source:
motif(Root, After, C, _, To, motif(creates_pin, Score, [Sq], pin(Kind, T, Sq, BT, BSq))) :-
    once(pin(After, pin(Kind, C, _, To, T, Sq, BT, BSq))),
    \+ pin(Root, pin(_, C, _, _, T, Sq, _, _)),
    (   Kind == absolute
    ->  Score = 250
    ;   Score = 180
    )
rules.summary: Only a NEW pin counts: sliding along a line that already pinned the piece (Bb5-a4 against a knight on c6) creates nothing.

rules.name: creates_skewer
rules.source:
motif(Root, After, C, _, To, motif(creates_skewer, 250, [FSq, BSq], skewer(FT, FSq, BT, BSq))) :-
    once(skewer(After, skewer(C, _, To, FT, FSq, BT, BSq))),
    \+ skewer(Root, skewer(C, _, _, FT, FSq, BT, BSq))
rules.summary: The moved piece skewers where it lands. As with pins, only a new skewer counts.

rules.name: hangs_piece
rules.source:
motif(Root, After, C, _, To, motif(hangs_piece, Score, [To], hangs(T, To))) :-
    at(After, To, C, T),
    T \== king,
    once(( is_hanging(After, C, T, To) ; is_threatened(After, C, T, To) )),
    captured_value(Root, To, C, VC),
    value(T, V),
    V > VC,
    Score is -120 * (V - VC)
rules.summary: The moved piece lands where it can be taken for less than it is worth.

rules.name: leaves_hanging
rules.source:
motif(Root, After, C, _, To, motif(leaves_hanging, Score, [Sq], leaves(T, Sq))) :-
    piece(After, C, T, Sq),
    Sq \== To,
    is_hanging(After, C, T, Sq),
    \+ is_hanging(Root, C, T, Sq),
    value(T, V),
    Score is -100 * V
rules.summary: Some other piece is undefended now but was not before (a defender left).

rules.name: rescues
rules.source:
motif(Root, After, C, From, To, motif(rescues, Score, [From], rescues(T, From))) :-
    at(Root, From, C, T),
    T \== king,
    once(( is_hanging(Root, C, T, From) ; is_threatened(Root, C, T, From) )),
    at(After, To, C, T2),
    \+ is_hanging(After, C, T2, To),
    \+ is_threatened(After, C, T2, To),
    value(T, V),
    Score is 80 * V
rules.summary: The moved piece was undefended or attacked by something cheaper, and where it lands it is neither.

rules.name: occupies_outpost
rules.source:
motif(_, After, C, _, To, motif(occupies_outpost, 120, [To], outpost(T, To))) :-
    at(After, To, C, T),
    memberchk(T, [knight, bishop]),
    opponent(C, O),
    once(is_weak_square(After, O, To, _))
rules.summary: A knight or bishop lands on a hole in the enemy camp.

rules.name: rook_to_open_file
rules.source:
motif(_, After, C, F0/_, F/R, motif(rook_to_open_file, Score, [F/R], file(F, Kind))) :-
    F \== F0,
    at(After, F/R, C, rook),
    (   is_open_file(After, F)
    ->  Score = 80, Kind = open
    ;   is_semi_open_file(After, C, F)
    ->  Score = 50, Kind = semi_open
    )
rules.summary: A rook changes file and lands on an open or semi-open one.

rules.name: pushes_passed_pawn
rules.source:
motif(Root, After, C, From, To, motif(pushes_passed_pawn, Score, [To], passed(To))) :-
    at(Root, From, C, pawn),
    at(After, To, C, pawn),
    is_passed(After, C, To),
    To = _/R,
    rel_rank(C, R, RR),
    Score is 30 + 15 * RR
rules.summary: A pawn moves and is a passed pawn where it lands. Worth more the further up the board it gets.

rules.name: win_material
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(win_material, Text, [Id], [ring(Sq, plan)])) :-
    opponent(S, O),
    member(Id-hanging(O, T, Sq, _), Facts),
    sq_name(Sq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Win material: the ~w on ~w is undefended.', [T, Name])
rules.summary: An enemy piece is undefended and can be taken.

rules.name: take_undefended
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(take_undefended, Text, [Id], [ring(GSq, plan)])) :-
    opponent(S, O),
    member(Id-pinned_defender(O, _, _, GT, GSq), Facts),
    sq_name(GSq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Take the ~w on ~w: its only defender is pinned to the king.', [GT, Name])
rules.summary: An enemy piece's only defender is pinned to its king.

rules.name: win_trapped_piece
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(win_trapped_piece, Text, [Id], [ring(Sq, plan)])) :-
    opponent(S, O),
    member(Id-trapped(O, T, Sq, _, _), Facts),
    sq_name(Sq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Win the ~w on ~w: it is attacked and has no safe square.', [T, Name])
rules.summary: An enemy piece is attacked and has no safe square.

rules.name: discovered_attack
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(discovered_attack, Text, [Id], [ring(MSq, plan), arrow(SSq, TSq, plan)])) :-
    member(Id-discovered_attack(S, MT, MSq, _, SSq, TT, TSq), Facts),
    sq_name(MSq, M), sq_name(TSq, T),
    format(atom(Text), 'Move the ~w from ~w with a threat of its own: that uncovers an attack on the ~w on ~w.',
           [MT, M, TT, T])
rules.summary: One of the mover's own pieces masks a line piece that would otherwise attack.

rules.name: queen_the_pawn
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(queen_the_pawn, Text, [Id], [ring(Sq, plan)])) :-
    member(Id-unstoppable_pawn(S, Sq), Facts),
    sq_name(Sq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Push the pawn on ~w: the enemy king cannot catch it.', [Name])
rules.summary: The mover has a pawn the enemy king cannot catch.

rules.name: save_piece
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(save_piece, Text, [Id], [ring(Sq, plan)])) :-
    (   member(Id-hanging(S, T, Sq, _), Facts)
    ;   member(Id-threatened(S, T, Sq, _, _), Facts)
    ),
    T \== pawn,
    sq_name(Sq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Deal with the threat to your ~w on ~w: move it or defend it.', [T, Name])
rules.summary: One of the mover's own pieces, not a pawn, is undefended or attacked by something cheaper.

rules.name: answer_tactic
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(answer_tactic, Text, [Id], [ring(From, plan)])) :-
    opponent(S, O),
    (   member(Id-fork(O, T, From, _), Facts), Name = fork
    ;   member(Id-skewer(O, T, From, _, _, _, _), Facts), Name = skewer
    ),
    sq_name(From, F),
    format(atom(Text), 'Answer the ~w from the ~w on ~w before anything else.', [Name, T, F])
rules.summary: The opponent has a fork or a skewer on the board.

rules.name: exploit_pin
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(exploit_pin, Text, [Id], [ring(Sq, plan)])) :-
    member(Id-pin(_, S, _, _, T, Sq, BT, _), Facts),
    sq_name(Sq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Pile up on the pinned ~w on ~w: it cannot move without exposing the ~w.',
           [T, Name, BT])
rules.summary: The mover is pinning an enemy piece.

rules.name: back_rank
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(back_rank, Text, [Id], [ring(KSq, plan)])) :-
    opponent(S, O),
    member(Id-weak_back_rank(O, KSq), Facts),
    sq_name(KSq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Look for a check along the back rank: the king on ~w has no escape square.', [Name])
rules.summary: The enemy king's back rank is weak.

rules.name: make_luft
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(make_luft, Text, [Id], [ring(KSq, plan)])) :-
    member(Id-weak_back_rank(S, KSq), Facts),
    sq_name(KSq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Give your king on ~w an escape square, or keep a rook on the back rank.', [Name])
rules.summary: The mover's own king's back rank is weak.

rules.name: use_outpost
rules.source:
plan(Ctx, S, Facts, plan(use_outpost, Text, [Id], [arrow(NSq, Sq, plan)])) :-
    opponent(S, O),
    member(Id-weak_square(O, Sq, _), Facts),
    \+ at(Ctx, Sq, S, _),
    once(piece(Ctx, S, knight, NSq)),
    sq_name(Sq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Route a knight to the outpost on ~w.', [Name])
rules.summary: There is a hole in the enemy camp that the mover does not occupy yet, and the mover has a knight.

rules.name: use_open_file
rules.source:
plan(Ctx, S, Facts, plan(use_open_file, Text, [Id], [file(F, plan)])) :-
    once(( member(Id-open_file(F), Facts),
           piece(Ctx, S, rook, _),
           \+ piece(Ctx, S, rook, F/_)
         )),
    file_letter(F, L),
    format(atom(Text), 'Put a rook on the open ~w-file.', [L])
rules.summary: A file is open and the mover has a rook, none of them on that file. Suggested for one file only.

rules.name: pawn_break
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(pawn_break, Text, [Id], [arrow(From, To, plan)])) :-
    member(Id-pawn_break(S, From, To, Target), Facts),
    sq_name(From, F), sq_name(To, T), sq_name(Target, G),
    format(atom(Text), 'Break with the pawn from ~w to ~w to challenge the pawn on ~w.', [F, T, G])
rules.summary: The mover has a pawn break available.

rules.name: push_passed_pawn
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(push_passed_pawn, Text, [Id], [ring(Sq, plan)])) :-
    member(Id-passed_pawn(S, Sq), Facts),
    sq_name(Sq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Advance the passed pawn on ~w and support it with pieces.', [Name])
rules.summary: The mover has a passed pawn.

rules.name: attack_king
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(attack_king, Text, [Id], [ring(KSq, plan)])) :-
    opponent(S, O),
    member(Id-king_shield(O, KSq, _), Facts),
    sq_name(KSq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Aim pieces at the king on ~w: its pawn cover is damaged.', [Name])
rules.summary: The enemy king is missing pawn cover.

rules.name: guard_king
rules.source:
plan(_, S, Facts, plan(guard_king, Text, [Id], [ring(KSq, plan)])) :-
    member(Id-king_shield(S, KSq, _), Facts),
    sq_name(KSq, Name),
    format(atom(Text), 'Your king on ~w is short of pawn cover: keep defenders close.', [Name])
rules.summary: The mover's own king is missing pawn cover.

rules.name: score
rules.summary: The value the alpha-beta search returned for the move, at the depth stated. A number from a search, not a judgement.

rules.name: line
rules.summary: The principal variation: the sequence of moves the search found best for both sides.

rules.name: material
rules.summary: The material count at the end of the search's line minus the count before it, for the side that moves first.

rules.name: level
rules.summary: Below full strength the engine may pass over its best move. The note says which move it found best and which it played.

rules.name: terms
rules.summary: The static evaluator's six terms for the position as it stands, before any move.

rules.name: ranking
rules.summary: Prolog's score for a move is the sum of the scores of its motifs. It is made without searching and the search does not use it.

rules.name: line_end
rules.summary: Prolog is asked about the position at the end of the search's line and its tactical facts are reported. That position may never arise.

rules.name: unavailable
rules.summary: Prolog did not answer in time or is not installed, so nothing symbolic is reported.

rules.name: verdict_bands
rules.summary: A move is rated by how much worse it scores than the search's choice at the same depth: up to 0.15 pawns about as good, up to 0.6 an inaccuracy, up to 2.0 a mistake, more a blunder. A move that gives up more than 0.6 but leaves its mover no worse is a missed chance.

rules.name: fact_delta
rules.summary: Prolog is asked about the position before the move and the position after it. A fact is new if its key appears only afterwards, gone if only before.

rules.name: plan_support
rules.summary: A plan keeps its support after a move if every fact it cites is still reported in the position after that move.

rules.name: is_check
rules.summary: A move Prolog says gives check is confirmed without a search: giving check is a property of the position after the move.

rules.name: material_gain
rules.summary: A motif that claims to win material is confirmed if the search's line ends at least one pawn of material ahead, and unconfirmed if it does not.

rules.name: capture_on_target
rules.summary: A fork, pin or skewer is confirmed if the mover later captures on one of its target squares in the search's line, and unconfirmed if not.

rules.name: warning
rules.summary: A Prolog warning about a move is confirmed if the search's line for that move ends at least one pawn of material down and the search rates the move worse than its best; unconfirmed if the search rates the move more than 0.6 pawns worse without that loss showing; overruled otherwise, including a sacrifice the search rates as its best.

rules.name: warning_played
rules.summary: A Prolog warning about the move the search chose is overruled: the search looked at the move and preferred it to every other.

rules.name: top_move
rules.summary: Prolog's highest-ranked move is compared with the move the search chose. If they differ, Prolog's suggestion is overruled.

rules.name: none
rules.summary: Positional advice. The search does not look far enough to confirm or refute it, so it is reported as a heuristic.
